newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower, Teva up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower, Teva up sharply.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower across the board on profit-taking as a sharp rise in blue chip Teva Pharmaceutical Industries prevented the market from falling further, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.29 percent, or 0.55 points, to 191.03 on turnover of 73 million shekels against 60 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.41 percent to 201.16.
"What we saw today was a technical correction. Only Teva's rise prevented the market from falling further," said a trader at First International Bank of Israel.
Teva, the most active share, gained 3.5 percent to 144,364 on high volume of 17 million shekels.
"There are rumours in the market that Teva will soon receive approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for a new generic drug," the trader said.

"After four days of nice gains the market had to slow down and investors took profits. A slight technical correction is unavoidable before another rise. The market was also reacting to news about difficulties in talks with the Palestinians," said Gidi Halpern at Meitav Investments.

U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross said he plans to leave the Middle East having failed to break a stalemate in Israeli-PLO talks after 15 days of trying. The announcement was made after the end of the trading day.

"The market will continue to rise if the Bank of Israel makes a significant interest rate cut and if the depreciation of the shekel continues. Investors are also waiting for a package deal that will include a major spending cut," Halpern said.
The Israeli shekel has lost more than two percent since last Wednesday on hopes that the Bank of Israel will cut interest rates next week. The key short-term rate is now 15.5 percent.
Africa Israel Investments lost 4.0 percent to 386,591 but traders noted that the share fell on a very low volume.
Other active shares include Koor Industries, which fell 0.75 percent to 29,715 on volume of 3.2 million shekels and Elite Industries, which rose 2.0 percent to 1,391 on volume of 3.1 million shekels.
